cutlass.result: CUTLASS supports H200 generally, but its inspected paged low-latency GQA example is Blackwell-specific; no exact SM90a d512 arbitrary-tree-mask drop-in was identified.

flashattention.result: The official CUDA FA2 surface supports head dimensions only through 256. The official FA4 d256/d512 roadmap targets SM100/SM110 Blackwell, not H200 SM90a, and does not prove the NGRAM full-mask tuple.

flashinfer.result: FlashInfer advertises paged/ragged attention and H200 support, but not every feature on every architecture; pinned Gemma4 explicitly excludes it and no exact d512/full-tree-mask adapter was proved.

sglang_current.result: Current upstream was inspected only for support context; the scientific source identity remains pinned v0.5.13.

closed_submechanisms.reason: Pinned Triton builds request/page/SWA/mask metadata once per ForwardBatch and reuses it across all 60 layers.
The qualified cache path is BF16 with no scale. FP8 cache changes stored K/V values and scale semantics, so it cannot preserve exact target logits for all admissible inputs.
No inspected proven implementation covers the complete H200 SM90a + page-size-1 NHD + BF16 + d256/d512 + GQA + local window + arbitrary NGRAM full-mask tuple.

hypothesis.causal_change: Flatten target-row x GQA-head into the attention M tile per request/KV-head CTA, load each paged K/V tile once for the group, and have q-tile-zero store the new normalized/rotated K/V to the future cache.
competing_explanations: Stock query-head CTAs may already reuse K/V through L2, leaving no material traffic reduction.
Global d512 grouped live state may spill or reduce residency enough to erase byte savings.
The bound qualified endpoint may have explicitly overridden the source-default backend; the permitted predecessor artifacts do not include an attention path marker.
Attention may be too small a critical-path share for a component gain to matter end to end.
hypothesis.predicted_movement: Lower L2 read sectors, one fewer launch per layer, unchanged per-row key traversal and online-softmax order, bitwise-identical attention/o_proj/logit/cache results.
hypothesis.stock_control: Pinned SGLang Triton TARGET_VERIFY: one store_cache launch plus one extend_attention_fwd launch per layer, grid=(request, query_head, ceil(12/BLOCK_M)).

resource_risk.global: About 128 KiB 32-bit register live state plus 64 KiB shared K/V tile per CTA before overhead; likely one CTA/SM and must be rejected on spills or >255 registers/thread.
resource_risk.local: About 48 KiB 32-bit register live state plus 64 KiB shared K/V tile per CTA before overhead.

whole_request_relevance.interpretation: Derived scale if all removable logical traffic reached HBM and bytes translated directly to time. It is not a performance prediction, measured gain, or strict upper bound.
whole_request_relevance.strict_upper_reason: The two permitted predecessor artifacts contain no attention timing or scope-matched critical-path attribution. Source counts cannot prove a tighter latency upper bound than the complete 0.625149101968745 s/request endpoint.

source_trace.backend_identity: Triton is the source-default Gemma4 backend on non-SM100 H200; actual qualified endpoint use remains inferred because the two bound artifacts contain no attention marker or explicit override.
